label: ORDER: The compiled routing order is DATA: registry-compiler.cjs copies hubRouter.routerPolicy.tieBreak into routingModel.tieBreak and derives bundleRules and compositionRules from it; no surface order is hardcoded in the compiled-routing runtime or the sk-code compiler.
ORDER: Runtime tie resolution consumes the same tieBreak data: equal scores sort by tieBreak index, bundles are ordered by it, and clarify alternatives are ranked by it.

ORDER: surfaceHint is a post-validation reorder implemented in code: applySurfaceHint promotes a hinted surface into the first surface slot, keeps workflow-mode slots, adds/drops no target, and only counts declared surface destinations.

ORDER (live): the front door routes 'obsidian plugin webflow implementation' as [sk-code-obsidian, sk-code-webflow] plain, and flips to [sk-code-webflow, sk-code-obsidian] under --surface-hint WEBFLOW or sk-code-webflow.
ORDER: order.cjs is a UTF-16 string comparator, not a surface rank; the file name invites misreading.

ORDER: A mode absent from routerPolicy.tieBreak has no rank: the order map and bundle rules are built only from tieBreak members, so a user-added surface must be added to tieBreak or it sorts unstably and never appears in a bundle rule.

ORDER: The committed compiled manifest stores policy identity only (effectivePolicyHash + generation + servingAuthority + shadowOnly); the surface order is re-derived at serve time from live hub inputs under a hash+generation identity binding.

PRESENCE: The canary corpus presumes obsidian and webflow are installed: expected outcomes include surface-bundle-obsidian, surface-collision-obsidian-over-webflow, single-obsidian, single-webflow, single-opencode, and webflow-hint cases.

PRESENCE: The compiler never checks packet existence: destinations come from registry.modes alone and minted inputs are only SKILL.md, hub-router.json, mode-registry.json; deleting the two surface packets while their entries remain still compiles a policy that routes to them.
PRESENCE: sk-code is default-on compiled and its manifest servingAuthority is compiled, so the policy naming the example surfaces is the default serving path, not an opt-in.
PRESENCE: No compiled-routing check tests surface-packet existence: the guard checks manifest validity, freshness and authored drift only; observed exit 0 with sk-code fresh.
PRESENCE: The hint capability is static per hub: the engine binds applySurfaceHint only when the hub's router module exports it, not on packet existence.

OK: Fail-safe serving: compiled is authoritative only when the flag permits, the manifest says compiled, and the routed snapshot's hash+generation match the manifest; otherwise null to the legacy sentinel.
OK: Hint semantics are matched-only: unmatched/UNKNOWN/unknown/empty hints change nothing, hubs without surfaces ignore hints, and a workflow mode keeps first place.

OK: Mint/refresh are lease-locked and atomic (temp-write + rename; refresh bumps generation, preserves servingAuthority); freshness = recompile-and-compare, preferring the shadow-child snapshot; all 7 hubs observed fresh.

OK: The sync tool promotes the runtime closure by tracing reads and copies only what the serving path touches; --check compares served copies to authored and writes nothing; its head enumerates no surface packets.

DOC: The promoted runtime is a byte-identical mirror of the authored program under specs/sk-doc/z_archive/019-skill-routing-refactor/015-router-unification-program; direct edits to .skilled/bin/lib/compiled-routing are reverted by rebuild/drift.
